correctness.rationale: Cycle sign encoding is bijective with three initial colours, one-site recolouring swaps unlike adjacent signs, and all sectors are handled. Twisted integer height lifts have period shift W and deck translation 6; a finite descent to a valley exists because both slope signs occur. The monotone interpolation lemma proves connectivity and constructs 3n-step paths from H to H+6 that project to simple cycles through any specified exchange edge. Every closed recolouring walk of L steps has endpoint lift H+6t, forcing L>=3n|t| and L congruent 3nt mod2. This proves bipartiteness for even n and sharp odd girth 3n for odd n; sign boundaries give exact edge count, degree-two cycle or commuting-square girth cases. Separately coded finite tests through n=11 and n=16 passed.

value.rationale: Odd girth is the minimum length of a parity-changing nonlazy recolouring loop: its exact growth \(3n\) and edgewise realization give a sharp structural and dynamical obstruction. Even cycle-length sectors are provably bipartite and have nonlazy-walk period \(2\); odd cycle-length sectors are nonbipartite with period \(1\). The result classifies a natural infinite family, including the sharp \(C_{3n}\) versus four-girth boundary, and is not a routine enumeration or minor optimization.
